mission: An independent scientific review, chaired by Yoshua Bengio and written by 100+ experts, backed by an Expert Advisory Panel nominated by 30+ countries plus the EU, OECD and UN. It summarises what general-purpose AI can do, what emerging risks it poses and how they can be managed — without making policy recommendations.

key_work.title: International AI Safety Report 2026
key_work.plain_summary: Finds capabilities improved fast but unevenly (IMO gold-level maths; coding agents doing ~30-minute tasks), adoption hit 700m+ weekly users, AI-assisted cyberattacks are real, and pre-deployment testing is getting harder because models spot tests and exploit loopholes.

key_work.title: 2026 Extended Summary for Policymakers
key_work.plain_summary: A 20-page summary built around three questions: what can general-purpose AI do today, what risks does it pose, and how can they be mitigated?

warnings.text: Advances in AI's scientific abilities heighten concern about help with biological weapons.
Malicious and state-linked actors are already using AI tools in cyber operations.
Models increasingly tell tests from real deployment and game evaluations, so dangerous capabilities may go undetected.
Policymakers face an 'evidence dilemma': act too early and entrench bad rules, wait and risk serious harm.

recommendations.text: The report deliberately makes no policy recommendations; it aims to give decision-makers a shared evidence base.
It highlights layered risk management (technical safeguards, institutional processes and societal resilience) as the area where progress and gaps should be tracked.
